title: C++ and RPC file handle EBADF behavior
scope: Namespace missing, closed, and foreign-World/revision handles report generic-category EBADF when handle validation is reached
Read through write-only handles and data write, writeback, append, truncate, or size setattr through read-only handles report EBADF
RPC handle ownership failures, including closed and foreign-session tokens, use typed wire code errno + 1
Failed access checks preserve committed namespace state, inode metadata, file data, and shared cursors; valid duplicate and owning handles remain usable
explicit_exclusions: Revision write policy and invalid/expired session errors retain existing behavior
Malformed payload, offset, and session validation precedence is unchanged
Read-only handles retain permitted owner metadata operations such as mode and time changes
Advisory locks remain available through read-only handles
No native FSKit errno mapping or general POSIX permission behavior is claimed

cpp_regression.observed: A read-only orphan write threw generic runtime_error instead of generic-category EBADF.

raw_rpc_regression.observed: A read-only fs-hwrite returned generic wire code 1 instead of EBADF + 1 (10).

fixed_validation.execution_controls: Disposable isolated executor; no-Git, read-only source snapshot; deny-default execution; isolated HOME/TMP; loopback-only tests. No native install, signing, secrets, push, or PR publication.

first_fixed_run.failure: The pre-existing symlink_handles.py foreign-session assertion expected generic wire code 1; the new EBADF + 1 result was intended. The assertion was corrected and the final full run passed.

review_scope.scope: Daemon C++ Namespace and raw RPC errno behavior only. Inode/handle identity mismatch semantics, revision write policy, resolver behavior, lock semantics, and native FSKit claims remain unchanged or excluded.
